methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series E → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.4x) to $27M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $2.0B - $2.3B.

private.name: Divergent
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series E), post-money $2.3B

data.narrative:
Fairmat, a Series E robotics and manufacturing company that has raised approximately $103M to date, is assessed against a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company in the sector. The three most proximate peers—Divergent (Series E, $2.3B), Exotec (Series D, $2.0B), and Locus Robotics (Series F, $2.0B)—anchor the market context.

Two valuation methods are applicable. The stage-progression approach, using total raised as a proxy base ($27M) and applying a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical for Series E advancement, implies $38M. The peer-median method, drawing on the three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, yields a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range of $2.0B to $2.3B. These methods produce materially divergent signals, reflecting the wide dispersion in peer outcomes at this stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $32M to $2.3B, with a median of $1.0B. The lower bound reflects stage-progression mechanics; the upper bound reflects peer multiples at comparable or slightly later stages. Key uncertainties driving this wide band include relative product maturity, customer concentration, and revenue scale relative to the peer set. Without disclosed financials, calibration to actual revenue multiples or path-to-profitability remains constrained. Further diligence on unit economics and customer retention would narrow this range materially.
